successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: Circassia conquered by Russia: the Kuban, Black Sea coast and Caucasus foothills, ended 21 May 1864

ledger.x: c. 1250: Circassia emerges as the land of the Circassian princes. Infobox 'Established: c. 13th century'; 1250 is the middle of the century and not a dated founding.
July 1763: Russia occupies Mozdok and the Russo-Circassian War begins.
1839: Bighuqal (Anapa) is declared the new capital of Circassia ('Hawduqo Mansur: declared leader of the confederation in 1839').
June 1860: the Circassian parliament meets at Sochi.
21 May 1864: Russia takes the rest of Circassia.

wars.name: Russo-Circassian War
wars.outcome: A hundred-year war: Russia occupied Mozdok (July 1763), put Kabarda under military rule (1822), claimed Circassia by the Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829), landed on the coast in 1838 and crushed the Circassians in the offensive of 1857-1864 (Abzakh…

wars.name: Kabardian refusal of Crimean and Ottoman tribute
wars.outcome: After Ottoman and Crimean tribute demands went unmet in 1708 the Kabardians declared they would never pay again and the Crimean forces were defeated.

certainty.note: A confederation of tribes: only the Kuban river line and the coast are firm; no page gives any survey line.
